newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa retains most gains, trade active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa retains most gains, trade active.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures retained most gains by the close on Tuesday although prices were below new intraday highs.
Traders said volume on the nearbys was inflated by switch trades.
Distant months were much stronger in the light of manufacturer demand and arbitrage buying against New York. Some origin sales were also seen.
Benchmark September finished at contract's high of 1,160 stg a tonne, up 10 stg on the day, after carving a new one-year peak at 1,170 stg. Its intraday low was 1,150.
"It's a positive close," said one trader.
July, which entered the month-long delivery period on Tuesday, was 14 stg ahead at 1,146 stg.
Some 4,000 lots were put up for tenders against July and, coupled with the dwindling open interest, this effectively finished the spot contract off.

The September contract surged early to a high of 1,169 after opening well above its previous resistance at 1,162. It gained further to 1,170 in the afternoon as rollercoaster New York cocoa hit a double top at $1,735, basis September.
The London market was just two stg away from its June 1996 high of 1,172 based on the second month continuation chart.
Traders said London's strength was also supported by the lack of nearby origin hedge selling as producers were well sold.
But industry generally was reluctant to follow, after having bought last week, and deterred by sterling's firmness against most European units.
Fundamentally, the market is still underpinned by concerns over the possible adverse impact of the El Nino weather pattern on the coming crop.
Traders were keeping an eye on second quarter European cocoa grind data due later this week or early next week.
Analysts said the figures were expected to show a mixed trend and would have little impact on the market.
